Controlled practical briefing

Unit 1 · Week 7 · Lesson 4 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Teacher supplies the fresh task, permitted resources, assessment conditions, submission location and marking materials separately. Public deck contains process guidance only.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Controlled practical briefing

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher-led assessment orientation

This is the existing Week 7 planner practical slot. Use the teacher-issued task and school assessment arrangements; do not treat this public deck as a complete assessment instrument. Keep the fresh scenario and marking materials in the teacher-controlled distribution channel. Suggested timing is a 55-minute session; adjust to the issued task.

2. Task and conditions

Suggested time: 4 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher-led briefing

Issue the fresh problem separately. Confirm permitted resources, collaboration/help rules, time available and what evidence must be submitted. Explain how students can request clarification of wording without receiving a solution. Do not show a worked answer during the controlled attempt. This slide introduces no new marks or weighting.

3. Requirements before code

Suggested time: 4 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual task reading

Students independently identify required inputs, processing, outputs and data/file formats from the issued brief. They should distinguish task requirements from assumptions and seek permitted clarification. Apply only the features actually required by the task, rather than adding unnecessary file operations or algorithms.

4. A plan you can explain

Suggested time: 7 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent planning

Students prepare a brief plan or pseudocode using only conventions/resources allowed in the task. Ask them to decide where selection, repetition, list processing or functions serve the actual problem. They record independent expected results before implementation. Teacher observation follows the issued assessment conditions.

5. Independent implementation

Suggested time: 20 minutes

Instructional strategy: Controlled individual work

Main implementation interval:20 suggested minutes. Students use the teacher-issued resources and follow its help rules. Teacher handles environment failures in accordance with the task conditions and keeps assessment observations separately. No model code or task-specific answers appear in the public deck.

6. Testing against the requirements

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent verification

Suggested 10-minute testing interval. Students compare prior expectations with actual results, include applicable normal/boundary/invalid/file cases and record corrections honestly. Which tests are required comes from the issued task. Preserve evidence of a mismatch and rerun rather than replacing expectations to match an error.

7. Submission check

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual submission review

Allow five suggested minutes for the issued submission procedure. Students verify their own final files open and the requested code/design/test evidence is included. Avoid adding criteria absent from the task. Keep original assessment evidence intact and follow the teacher’s submission directions.

8. Reflection after submission

Suggested time: 3 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual reflection and teacher follow-up

After the controlled attempt ends, students reflect without changing submitted evidence. Teacher decides when task-specific feedback or solutions may be discussed, especially if other classes still need to complete it. Use observations to plan Week 8 design/testing support rather than adding another assessment.
